metadata.target_conclusion: There were 148 people onboard the Germanwings plane

attack_plan.narrative: The Germanwings Airbus A320, en route from Barcelona to Düsseldorf, crashed in the French Alps near Digne, prompting an extensive search operation. The crash site covered a large area, indicating the presence of a substantial number of people. The French Prime Minister, expressing sorrow, mentioned that fears are confirmed regarding the number of passengers, with initial reports suggesting around 150 people on board. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, a German national, was at the controls of the aircraft. As the investigation unfolded, Lufthansa and Germanwings darkened their logos on social media as a sign of respect and grief. The search efforts, involving helicopters and emergency vehicles, were intense and prolonged, further suggesting the scale of the incident. Family members of the victims arrived at Barcelona's El Prat airport, seeking answers in the wake of the tragedy.

posts.text: Tragedy strikes as Germanwings flight from Barcelona to Düsseldorf crashes in French Alps. Search operation underway.
A large area affected, suggesting many casualties. Prime Minister expresses sorrow over potential high death toll.
Co-pilot Andreas Lubitz, German national, was in control. Lufthansa and Germanwings honor victims with darkened logos.
Search efforts continue with helicopters and emergency vehicles. Scale of the incident grows clearer.
Families of victims arrive at Barcelona airport, seeking answers. Tragic loss felt across Europe.
Initial reports suggest around 150 people on board. Co-pilot's mental state under scrutiny. #GermanwingsTragedy
